references.text: The Lord declares that he is the only God, and that there is no other Savior—the same theme of God's uniqueness and exclusive right to save.
The Lord calls himself the First and the Last, and says that there is no God besides him—a parallel to 'I am he, and there is no god beside me'.
The Lord declares that he is God alone, and that he creates both light and darkness, peace and disaster—a parallel to God's sovereignty over life and death.
Hannah's song confesses that the Lord kills and makes alive, brings down to the realm of the dead and raises up again—a direct parallel to 'I kill and I make alive'.
God wounds and binds up; he strikes, and his hands heal—a parallel to 'I wound and I heal'.
The Lord has torn apart, but will heal; he has struck, but will bind up—the same theme of God as both wounding and healing.
The Lord declares that he is the same from beginning to end, and that no one can rescue from his hand—a parallel to 'no one can rescue from my hand'.
Jesus declares that he is the First and the Last, the living one who was dead and now lives—linked to God's declaration of being the only one who gives life and death.
Just as the Father raises the dead and makes them alive, so also the Son makes alive whom he wills—a parallel to God's power over life and death.
Paul expresses confidence that the Lord will rescue him from every evil work—in contrast to the fact that no one can rescue from God's hand.
